metadata.pack_name: V29 Unified Hostile Audit Remediation Pack

severity_scale.P0: Blocks submission or causes runtime failure
severity_scale.P1: Materially weakens submission credibility or creates latent data corruption risk
severity_scale.P2: Convention drift or maintainability drag that compounds over time
severity_scale.P3: Cosmetic or low-risk items addressable post-submission

issues.title: Repo tells four different snapshot dates
issues.description: README.md references 20260323, PACK_MANIFEST.json references 20260324, 00_START_HERE.md references 20260328, STATUS_DASHBOARD.md references 2026-03-23-hardening-closeout. A DARPA reviewer opening the repo sees conflicting provenance.
issues.fix: Rewrite README.md, PACK_MANIFEST.json, SOURCE_BASIS.md, STATUS_DASHBOARD.md to reference the current snapshot date and archive name. Archive all superseded versions.
issues.acceptance: All four files reference the same snapshot identifier and date. No stale snapshot references in any active document.

issues.title: 78 root-level control documents create archaeological confusion
issues.description: The repo root contains 78 markdown/JSON control documents including multiple numbered issue matrices (01_ through 17_), multiple playbooks, multiple source basis docs, and multiple status dashboards from different audit generations. A new maintainer or reviewer cannot identify which documents are authoritative.
evidence: Multiple 0X_ prefixed docs spanning at least 17 generations
CANONICAL_STACK_SPEC exists in V6, V7, V25, V26 variants
issues.fix: Move all superseded numbered docs and old canonical specs to docs/archive/. Keep exactly one active set: 00_START_HERE.md, README.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, PROMPT.md, Makefile, Cargo.toml, and the canonical spec. Create docs/archive/SUPERSESSION_INDEX.md listing what was archived and why.
issues.acceptance: Root directory contains <20 active control documents. Every archived doc is listed in the supersession index.

issues.title: Missing archive manifest artifact
issues.description: STATUS_EVIDENCE_MANIFEST.json references docs/archive/root_closeout_history/manifest.json but this file does not exist. The check_root_archive_manifest.py gate fails.
issues.fix: Generate the archive manifest from current state or update STATUS_EVIDENCE_MANIFEST.json to remove the stale reference.

issues.title: 6 target-* directories pollute the archive
issues.description: target-closeout-check, target-closeout-verify, target-full, target-serial, target-serial2, target-vc are build/test artifact directories that should not be in the source archive.
issues.fix: Add target-* to .gitignore and exclude from archive generation script (zip.py).
issues.acceptance: No target-* directories in the clean archive.

issues.title: check_commit_permit_paths.py expects wrong permit type
issues.description: The gate script expects ExecutionPermit in llm-tool-runtime signatures but the actual type is ToolExecutionPermit. The regex pattern in the script does not match the code.
issues.fix: Update the regex patterns in check_commit_permit_paths.py to match ToolExecutionPermit. Verify all pattern assertions against current code.

issues.title: check_hotspot_budgets.sh has contradictory limits for same file
issues.description: forge-pilot/src/main_support/mod.rs is checked twice: once at 1900 (line 57) and once at 1600 via check_documented_exception (line 62). The file is 1588 lines, so it passes the 1900 check but the 1600 documented-exception check may fail depending on whether the exception doc exists. knowledge-runtime/src/runtime/core.rs is similarly checked at 1400 and 1250.
evidence: main_support/mod.rs: 1588 lines (passes 1900, fails 1600 without exception doc)
issues.fix: Deduplicate entries. Use a single budget per file with the documented-exception mechanism for any file above 1000 lines.
issues.acceptance: bash scripts/check_hotspot_budgets.sh passes. No file is checked at two different limits.

issues.title: 12 stale versioned gate scripts
issues.description: Scripts referencing old pack versions (v9, v10, v11, v15, v16-v20, v21-v24) remain in scripts/ and create confusion about which gates are active.
issues.fix: Move stale versioned scripts to scripts/archive/. Ensure release_gate_set.py only references current scripts.
issues.acceptance: No check_v{N}_* scripts in active scripts/ directory. release_gate_set.py references only current gates.

issues.title: 56 serializable enums missing rename_all
issues.description: 56 enums with Serialize derive lack #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]. These serialize variants in PascalCase. If any data has been persisted, adding rename_all later will break deserialization. This must be decided NOW before CLARA submission creates persisted data.
evidence: Full list includes: ActionFamily, HaltReason, TargetKind, TargetPriority (forge-pilot)
ExperimentMode, EffectKind, TrialSide, FailureClass, 13 evidence.rs enums (living-memory)
6 enums in attestation-exchange, 3 in verification-policy, 2 in remote-oracle-admission
issues.fix: Add #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")] to all 56 enums. Since no production data has been persisted yet (pre-CLARA), this is safe. Document the convention enforcement in CLAUDE.md.
issues.acceptance: grep scan finds 0 serializable enums without rename_all in workspace members.

issues.title: Error-swallowing .ok() calls in semantic-memory production paths
issues.description: 25 .ok() calls in production code silently discard Results. Most are defensible (quantization fallback), but ~8 in db.rs, episodes.rs, knowledge.rs discard SQLite operation results that could mask data corruption.
issues.fix: Audit each .ok() call. For SQLite write operations, replace with tracing::warn! on error. For quantization fallback and feature-gated suppression, document with // INTENTIONAL: reason comment.
issues.acceptance: Every .ok() in production code has either been replaced with error logging or has an INTENTIONAL comment.

issues.title: Doc comment coverage below DARPA review threshold
issues.description: Average doc comment coverage across workspace crates is ~45%. DARPA-facing crates are worse: forge-pilot 38%, effect-runtime 34%, forge-memory-bridge 14%. cargo doc output will show a wall of undocumented types.
issues.fix: Add /// doc comments to all pub struct, pub enum, and pub trait declarations in the 17 supported-lane crates. Focus on types that cross crate boundaries first. Module-level //! docs on all lib.rs files.
files_touched: All files with undocumented pub types
issues.acceptance: Doc coverage exceeds 80% on pub struct/enum/trait across supported-lane crates.

issues.title: README.md is a stale pack description, not a project README
issues.description: README.md describes a remediation pack ('finish_pack_2026-03-24') rather than the RecursiveIntell library stack. A DARPA reviewer landing on this repo sees pack internals rather than a project description.
issues.fix: Rewrite README.md as a proper project README: what RecursiveIntell is, what the stack does, crate architecture overview, build instructions, and a link to the canonical spec.
issues.acceptance: README.md describes the project, not a remediation pack. Contains build instructions and architecture summary.

issues.title: 33 HashMap references in production code violate BTreeMap convention
issues.description: Project convention is BTreeMap everywhere for deterministic ordering. 33 HashMap references remain in production code across semantic-memory (HNSW, search, graph), knowledge-runtime (registry, lifecycle), and discovery-portfolio.
issues.fix: HNSW HashMap usage is architecturally justified (O(1) lookup, no ordering needed) — document with // CONVENTION EXCEPTION: reason. Convert remaining HashMaps in knowledge-runtime and discovery-portfolio to BTreeMap.
issues.acceptance: All HashMap usage is either converted to BTreeMap or documented with a CONVENTION EXCEPTION comment.

issues.title: Governance observation pipeline is thin relative to governance surface area
issues.description: governance_gate.rs observes 6 predicates (effect_preflight, assurance_ready, authority_delegation_valid, continuity_incident_active, constitutional_amendment_pending, mechanism_fit). But the governance crates define dozens of additional types (AttestationEnvelopeV1, MechanismBundleV1, AssuranceCaseV1, etc.) that are never observed. The pipeline is wired but the observation window is narrow.
evidence: mechanism-runtime: 9 pub types, only mechanism_fit observed
assurance-runtime: types exist but not individually observed
issues.fix: Document the current observation scope in governance_gate.rs module docs. Add TODO comments for future expansion. This is NOT a P0 — the 6 predicates cover the decision-relevant surfaces. Document the intentional narrowing.
issues.acceptance: Module docs explicitly state which governance surfaces are observed and which are deferred.

issues.title: attestation-exchange is optional and completely unconsumed
issues.description: attestation-exchange is an optional dependency in forge-pilot but no code imports or references any of its types. The trust-root validation story exists as types but has zero integration path.
issues.fix: Document in SCOPE_NOTES.md that attestation-exchange is a forward-declared surface not yet integrated into the observation pipeline. This is acceptable for CLARA V1.
issues.acceptance: SCOPE_NOTES.md explicitly acknowledges the attestation-exchange integration gap.

issues.title: No canonical performance evidence artifact
issues.description: The stack has performance benchmarking machinery (scripts/collect_canonical_perf_baseline.sh, kernel-conformance/examples/canonical_perf_snapshot.rs) but no current, committed performance evidence artifact.
evidence: No perf_baseline.json or equivalent in the repo
issues.fix: Run the canonical perf baseline and commit the result as evidence/perf_baseline_20260330.json.
issues.acceptance: A dated performance baseline artifact exists and is referenced from STATUS_DASHBOARD.md.

issues.title: check_no_prod_panics.sh allowlist is empty but panic audit may have false edges
issues.description: The panic checker uses an awk-based #[cfg(test)] skipper which is good, but the checker also excludes only files named tests.rs/lib_tests.rs/*_tests.rs. Files with inline test modules at the bottom get the awk treatment, but the awk parser counts braces which can be confused by string literals containing braces.
issues.fix: Verify the awk parser handles all current source files correctly by running the check. If false positives emerge, add to allowlist with justification comments in the JSON.
issues.acceptance: bash scripts/check_no_prod_panics.sh passes with 0 or documented allowlisted items.

tensor.delta_interpretation: Claude audit finds lower code/architecture risk than GPT (confirming the GOV-001/GOV-002 fixes landed), but agrees on ops/truth severity. The combined picture: architecture is strong, meta-layer is the bottleneck.
